principles: Local system communications are effectively routine; interstellar communication is constrained enough that ships and scheduled relays still matter.
Market data has an age. The farther outward a captain travels, the less confidence they should have that a quoted price or berth condition is still current.
Emergency communication improves the chance someone knows you are in trouble; it does not guarantee rescue.

services.name: Concord Relay Network
services.description: Commercial message forwarding and authenticated market-data distribution.

services.name: Meridian Packet
services.description: Store-and-forward traffic connecting Port Meridian, Talos, Waystation and Lastlight; delays and outages are ordinary enough that businesses plan around them.

services.name: Survey Burst
services.description: Compressed expedition reports transmitted when geometry and power allow; full datasets often return physically aboard ships.

radio_phrases.use: General local call when maneuvering near poorly controlled frontier sites.
Ship waiting powered and ready but not actively maneuvering, often for berth/weather clearance.
Loadmaster confirmation that cargo restraint and hazardous-cargo checks are complete.
Informal crew announcement before EVA; normally followed by suit/channel identification.
Crew member switching from shipwide/intercom to a local work channel.
Informal confirmation that pressure, power, temperature or other expected readings are within limits.

message_examples.text: Meridian Traffic, independent freighter Paid For, inbound from Waystation, forty-six standard containers, no declared hazard, requesting commercial berth.
Survey House, Narrow Arc filing outbound. Lantern direct, then Cairn. Planned return window twenty-two standard days. Four crew, reserves thirty-four.
Hopewell Field to Mule Four-Seven: hold north of marker three. Pad crew is still clearing dust and somebody left a loader where your landing gear wants to be.
